native_source_references.finding: R uses native room, session, caller, battery, human and all-Kirbys-same-room conditions. Mini is excluded, but UFO is not.
Ordinary UFO movement calls the common R macro and the native L path. L requires room priority 0x40 and ordinary session/single-player conditions.
R and L explicitly support UFO call animations. R initiation decrements battery. Holding L uses the separate return path.
Room-entry processing clears UFO when destination is 0x321, native 801. This is independent of Phone ownership.
L sets destination 801 and native warp-star return/control states.
300 is AI_KIRBY_STATE_NORMAL, a native progression state, not human-player count.
The native Central Circle cutscene advances AI progression to 300 and saves WORLD state.
The experimental hook guards only R entry 0x08056C2C. Native L entry 0x08056E40 is separate.
Production enable remains 0. The isolated fixture sets 1 before boot.
The real ownership queue requires complete history, compatible capability, ROM identity and stable native-file fences.

limits: This is a qualified native file 0 fixture, not a complete Central Circle-to-source progression route. Startup uses the decoded 734-to-720 left-arrival compartment; actual inputs then enter 730 through the original top door.

Every run begins from a blank native battery with AI progression 0. The first return to 801 triggers the ordinary Central Circle cutscene and advances AI progression to 300. This is explicitly not a post-tutorial AI 300 source approach.

The source policy is one current production full 25-ability per-enemy-type shuffle, seed 8, policy seed 5662892934360856578, no-ability weight 0. Ability gating and Area Keys are OFF; health is minimum = maximum = 6 and enemy health 100%. No arbitrary seed, ability, health or RoomSanity matrix is claimed.

R proves permission, battery use, UFO preservation and helper arrival under these conditions. It does not prove a helper attack, switch, block, collectible or route, nor that Phone is necessary for a target.

Only eight production source-configuration writes and, in owned cases, two guarded Phone queue writes occur. No runtime pose, HP, ability, helper equipment, battery, direct ownership or selected-file injection occurs; no state loads occur.
Validation uses a real native mGBA bridge with a transport adapter and complete synthetic server histories. No live AP server, full watcher or native BizHawk Lua transport is claimed.

Production Phone stays absent from generated slot capability and item pool/catalog. The experiment adds compatible Phone capability only to its isolated client context and changes the fixture enable word before boot.

The native L/return state range and room-entry UFO-clearing range are byte-identical to retail. UFO movement also retains existing production button-transition hooks; the entire UFO code range is not claimed to be pristine retail.

Two preliminary assertions were corrected: first-hub settle needed 1,500 rather than 300 frames, and native AI progression must be allowed to advance to 300. A preliminary telemetry label confused Copy dirty with owned; all six final accepted runs were cold-replayed with separate correct fields. Only final accepted-* runs are included.
ROMs, saves, screenshots, full traces, complete transport reads and generated archives remain private. This document contains only sanitized metadata and telemetry.
